hints: Give every possible index a distinct binary label.
One question can reveal one bit of every hidden index at once.
Ask one query per bit of i-1 and combine response bits at each output position.
analogy: Each position carries a barcode; the judge permutes the barcode stripes in the same way every time.
example: For n=3, labels 00,01,10 identify indices 1,2,3; responses at an output position reveal its label and therefore its index.
algorithm: For each bit b needed to represent n-1, send a binary string whose i-th bit is bit b of i-1. Flush and read the returned string. At each output position collect its returned bits into a number and add one. Print all recovered indices after ! and terminate. For n=1 output 1 without queries.
correctness: The returned bit at output position j is the bit assigned to index a[j]. Across all questions these bits form the unique binary representation of a[j]-1, so every permutation entry is recovered.
complexity: For n<=1000, ceil(log2 n)<=10 queries, O(n log n) local work and O(n) space.
